The Challenges of Heavy Tube Cutting
When running high-volume tube cutting lines, fabricators face massive setup bottlenecks:
Massive Dust & Slag Volumetrics: Continuous tube piercing produces high volumes of fine metallic dust and fumes that can clog standard shops and breach local EPA/municipal environmental bylaws.
Heavy Component Loads: Automatic loaders and bundle racks weigh tons, requiring reinforced shop floors and heavy-duty overhead structural support.
High Sparks & Fire Hazard: Intense sparks entering the exhaust ductwork pose a severe fire risk to the filter elements.

Our 4-in-1 Turnkey Solution

We eliminate these bottlenecks by wrapping the machine sale inside a complete local engineering package:

🇨🇦 Local CSA Certification & Machine Setup
We import, install, and commission your Longxin Laser.
We handle local CSA/ESA electrical certification modifications so your equipment is 100% legal to operate on the North American grid.
🌬️ Advanced Fume Extraction & PCU Systems
We design and install heavy-duty Pollution Control Units (PCUs) and dust collectors matched to Longxin’s exact CFM airflow requirements. Multi-stage filtration safely captures sub-micron metal dross and eliminates odors.
🛠️ CWB CSA W47.1 Division 2 Structural Fabrication
As a certified CWB Division 2 company, our in-house Professional Welding Engineer designs and fabricates structural steel roof platforms (dunnage) for giant exhaust fans, crane gantries, and automated storage racks.
🔥 Automatic Fire Suppression & CNC Interlocks
We install certified fire suppression systems inside the ductwork and dust collection chambers. If a spark triggers a thermal event, the system immediately trips the Longxin CNC controller to auto-shut down machine power and drop the fire lines instantly (Compliant with local fire codes).

Preventative Maintenance & SLA Support

Chuck calibration, rail lubrication, and laser source preventative health checks by factory-trained technicians.

entry.title: Make-up Air (MUA) Systems
entry.content:
Direct Gas-Fired MUA: We install and service TSSA-approved MUA units that heat freezing sub-zero outdoor air to a comfortable 20°C before bringing it into your kitchen.

Air Balancing: Maintaining an 80%-90% airflow replenishment to keep a perfect indoor pressure.

Technical Features & Selection

1)CFM Matching ：According to NFPA 96 and Ontario Building Code (OBC), the make-up air volume typically needs to reach 80% to 90% of the exhaust air volume (to maintain a slight negative pressure in the kitchen and prevent cooking fumes from entering the lobby).

2)Interlock System( )：Emphasis is placed on coordinated control. When the exhaust fan is turned on, the MUA automatically starts; when the exhaust fan is turned off, the MUA automatically turns off.
3)VFD - Variable Frequency Drive ：It supports automatic adjustment of air volume based on the intensity of cooking in the kitchen, helping the owner save electricity and gas.

    Professional Installation: Our experienced technician team handles rigging, duct connections, electrical wiring, and fan balancing.
